title: Limits by direct substitution
summary: For a polynomial, the limit at a finite real point equals its value there because polynomials are continuous.
concept: For a polynomial, the limit at a finite real point equals its value there because polynomials are continuous.

steps: Substitute $x=2$ because this polynomial is continuous.
example.check: The limit is $11$. Check by evaluating the polynomial at 2.

guardrail: Direct substitution requires continuity at the approach point.

title: Removable discontinuity and factoring
summary: When substitution gives $0/0$, simplify the expression on the punctured domain before taking the limit.
concept: When substitution gives $0/0$, simplify the expression on the punctured domain before taking the limit.

steps: For $x\ne3$ cancel the common factor; then take the limit of $x+3$.
example.check: The limit is $6$, although the original expression is undefined at $x=3$.

guardrail: Cancellation does not make the original function defined at the excluded point.

title: One-sided limits and continuity
summary: A two-sided limit exists only when both one-sided limits exist and agree.
concept: A two-sided limit exists only when both one-sided limits exist and agree.

example.prompt: For $f(x)=1$ when $x<0$ and $f(x)=2$ when $x\ge0$, determine the limit at 0.
steps: Approaching from the right gives 2; the one-sided values differ.
example.check: The two-sided limit does not exist.

guardrail: Continuity additionally requires the function value to equal the common limit.

title: Power and chain rules
summary: The chain rule differentiates an outer function then multiplies by the derivative of its inner function.
concept: The chain rule differentiates an outer function then multiplies by the derivative of its inner function.

steps: Take the derivative of the outer cube: $3(2x^2+1)^2$.

guardrail: Do not omit the inner derivative.

title: Implicit differentiation
summary: When a curve is defined implicitly, differentiate both sides and collect terms involving $y'$.
concept: When a curve is defined implicitly, differentiate both sides and collect terms involving $y'$.
guardrail: At points with $y=0$, this formula is undefined and the circle has vertical tangents.

title: Optimization by derivatives
summary: At an interior differentiable local extremum, the derivative is zero; endpoints and non-differentiable points also require checks.
concept: At an interior differentiable local extremum, the derivative is zero; endpoints and non-differentiable points also require checks.

example.prompt: Find the maximum of $A(x)=12x-x^2$ for $0\le x\le12$.
steps: Set $A'=0$ to obtain $x=6$, and compare the endpoints.

guardrail: A stationary point alone does not guarantee a maximum.

title: Second derivatives
summary: The second derivative measures the instantaneous change of the first derivative.
concept: The second derivative measures the instantaneous change of the first derivative.
guardrail: Repeated differentiation changes the exponent and coefficient each time.

title: Motion and acceleration
summary: For a position function, velocity is its first time derivative and acceleration is its second.
concept: For a position function, velocity is its first time derivative and acceleration is its second.

example.check: Acceleration is $18$ distance-units per time-unit squared.

guardrail: Signed acceleration is not the same as speed.

title: Leibniz rule for products
summary: The nth derivative of a product is a sum of derivatives weighted by binomial coefficients.
concept: The nth derivative of a product is a sum of derivatives weighted by binomial coefficients.
guardrail: Check all binomial terms; the middle term has coefficient 2.

title: Parametric first derivative
summary: For parametric coordinates $x(t)$ and $y(t)$, the curve slope is the ratio of time derivatives when $dx/dt\ne0$.
concept: For parametric coordinates $x(t)$ and $y(t)$, the curve slope is the ratio of time derivatives when $dx/dt\ne0$.
guardrail: The formula is undefined when $dx/dt=0$; investigate such parameters separately.

title: Parametric second derivative
summary: Differentiate the parametric slope with respect to $t$, then divide by $dx/dt$ again.
concept: Differentiate the parametric slope with respect to $t$, then divide by $dx/dt$ again.

steps: Differentiate with respect to $t$ and divide by $dx/dt=1$.

guardrail: Do not differentiate $dy/dx$ with respect to $t$ without dividing by $dx/dt$.

title: Tangents to a parametric curve
summary: At a regular point, use the parametric derivative to find the tangent slope and point.
concept: At a regular point, use the parametric derivative to find the tangent slope and point.

example.prompt: For $x=t^2$, $y=t^3$, give the tangent line at $t=1$.

guardrail: At nonregular points, slope formulas require separate analysis.

title: First partial derivatives
summary: Differentiate with respect to one variable while holding the other variables constant.
concept: Differentiate with respect to one variable while holding the other variables constant.
guardrail: Keep other independent variables constant while differentiating.

title: Higher mixed partials
summary: Under appropriate continuity conditions, mixed second partials commute.
concept: Under appropriate continuity conditions, mixed second partials commute.
guardrail: Equality of mixed partials is not unconditional at singular points.

title: Total differential
summary: The first-order differential approximates the total change due to changes in all independent variables.
concept: The first-order differential approximates the total change due to changes in all independent variables.

steps: Multiply by $dx$ and $dy$ respectively, then add.

guardrail: The differential approximates finite changes when increments are small.

title: Antiderivatives and constant of integration
summary: An indefinite integral represents a family of functions with the same derivative.
concept: An indefinite integral represents a family of functions with the same derivative.

steps: Increase the power by one and divide by the new exponent.

guardrail: Include the arbitrary constant $C$ for indefinite integrals.

title: Definite integrals and the FTC
summary: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus evaluates a definite integral using an antiderivative.
concept: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus evaluates a definite integral using an antiderivative.
guardrail: A definite integral represents signed accumulation, not always geometric area.

title: Riemann-sum interpretation
summary: A definite integral is the limit of sums of sample values times interval widths, when the limit exists.
concept: A definite integral is the limit of sums of sample values times interval widths, when the limit exists.

example.prompt: Find $\int_0^1 x\,dx$ using the right-endpoint sum idea.
steps: The sum becomes $n(n+1)/(2n^2)$, whose limit is $1/2$.

guardrail: This derivation assumes the stated equal partitions and sampling rule.

title: Substitution
summary: When the derivative of an inner expression is present, substitution simplifies the integral.
concept: When the derivative of an inner expression is present, substitution simplifies the integral.
guardrail: For definite integrals, change limits if retaining the substitution variable.
reference: Rohde Introduction to Integral Calculus; Larson 10th; Schaum's Calculus 5th

title: Integration by parts
summary: The integration-by-parts formula follows from the product rule.
concept: The integration-by-parts formula follows from the product rule.
guardrail: Choose factors that simplify the remaining integral.
reference: Rohde Introduction to Integral Calculus; Larson 10th; Schaum's Calculus 5th

title: Partial fractions
summary: A proper rational function can often be decomposed before integration, after polynomial division if necessary.
concept: A proper rational function can often be decomposed before integration, after polynomial division if necessary.

example.check: Answer: $\ln|x+1|-\ln|x+2|+C$, on a domain excluding $-1$ and $-2$.

guardrail: State excluded denominator zeros.
reference: Rohde Introduction to Integral Calculus; Larson 10th; Schaum's Calculus 5th

title: Infinite upper limits
summary: Replace an infinite bound by a finite bound and evaluate the limit.
concept: Replace an infinite bound by a finite bound and evaluate the limit.
guardrail: A finite antiderivative expression is not sufficient without the limiting step.

title: The p-test for improper integrals
summary: Power functions over unbounded intervals have a sharp convergence threshold.
concept: Power functions over unbounded intervals have a sharp convergence threshold.
guardrail: Do not apply the finite-interval power rule without checking limits.

title: Interior singularities
summary: Split an integral at every interior singularity and check each one-sided improper integral separately.
concept: Split an integral at every interior singularity and check each one-sided improper integral separately.

steps: Split at $x=0$, where the integrand is undefined.
Both one-sided integrals grow without bound.

guardrail: Do not cancel divergent contributions or use a principal value as the ordinary improper integral.

title: Area between curves
summary: The area between an upper curve and a lower curve is the integral of their difference on intervals with consistent ordering.
concept: The area between an upper curve and a lower curve is the integral of their difference on intervals with consistent ordering.

example.prompt: Find the area between $y=2x$ and $y=x^2$ for $0\le x\le2$.

guardrail: Confirm the upper curve; split the interval if curves swap order.

title: Solids of revolution
summary: For revolution about the x-axis, disks or washers use cross-sectional area.
concept: For revolution about the x-axis, disks or washers use cross-sectional area.

example.prompt: Find the volume formed by revolving $y=x$, $0\le x\le1$, about the x-axis.
steps: The disk radius is $R(x)=x$ and the inner radius is zero.

guardrail: Verify the axis of rotation and which radius is outer versus inner.

title: Charge from time-varying current
summary: Charge transferred over a time interval is the time integral of current, with units ampere-seconds = coulombs.
concept: Charge transferred over a time interval is the time integral of current, with units ampere-seconds = coulombs.

example.prompt: If $i(t)=2t$ amperes for $0\le t\le3$ seconds, find transferred charge.

guardrail: Current may be signed; net charge is not total unsigned charge flow.

title: Double integrals over rectangles
summary: An iterated integral accumulates a two-variable function over a region.
concept: An iterated integral accumulates a two-variable function over a region.
guardrail: Keep the order of differential symbols consistent with the bounds.

title: Reversing the order
summary: The same region can often be described by either integration order.
concept: The same region can often be described by either integration order.
guardrail: Sketch or characterize the region before changing bounds.

title: Triple integrals and volume
summary: The triple integral of one over a solid region gives its volume.
concept: The triple integral of one over a solid region gives its volume.

example.prompt: Compute the volume of the box $0\le x\le2$, $0\le y\le3$, $0\le z\le4$.
steps: Integrate $1$ over the stated Cartesian intervals.

guardrail: More general solids require bounds that reflect the geometry.
